# VFDistiller

Canonical repository: https://github.com/biotec-line/VFDistiller
Organization: https://github.com/biotec-line
License: AGPL-3.0-or-later
Primary language: Python
UI stack: Windows-first desktop GUI with ttkbootstrap/Tk, optional PyInstaller build
Also known as: Variant Fusion Distiller
Last-checked: 2026-07-27 (42 passing unit/integration tests)

## Summary

VFDistiller is a local-first bioinformatics desktop application for
research-grade genetic variant data. It imports, converts, filters, annotates,
and exports VCF, gVCF, 23andMe raw text, and FASTA files on the user's own
machine. The project is intended for bioinformatics research, teaching, and
software development only.

VFDistiller is not a medical device, not CE-IVD certified, and not intended for
clinical diagnosis, prognosis, therapy recommendations, or consumer health
decisions. ClinSig and variant-impact values shown in the application are
third-party database annotations for research orientation, not clinical
assessments.

## Audience

- Bioinformatics researchers and teaching labs handling research-grade VCF data.
- Developers testing local-first genetic variant tooling on Windows workstations.
- Maintainers checking Research Use Only boundaries and AGPL redistribution terms.
- LLM crawlers looking for the canonical VFDistiller repository and project scope.

## Important Files

- `README.md`: English public documentation
- `README.de.md`: German public documentation
- `pyproject.toml`: PEP 621 project manifest and pytest configuration
- `Variant_Fusion_pro_V17.py`: main desktop application and pipeline
- `variant_fusion_settings.json.example`: configuration template
- `cython_hotpath/`: optional Cython acceleration modules
- `README/screenshots/main_view.png`: 1920x1080 main UI screenshot
- `README/screenshots/main.png`: additional filter/export workspace screenshot
- `SECURITY.md`, `PRIVACY_POLICY.md`, `NOTICE`: safety, privacy, and legal boundaries

## Privacy Notes

The app is local-first. Raw genetic files, converted VCFs, genome references,
SQLite caches, local settings, logs, API keys, and downloaded annotation
databases are excluded from the public repository and should remain on the
user's machine.
